question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{5-\sqrt{3x+25}}{x} & =\frac{5-\sqrt{3(0)+25}}{0}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the numerator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{5-\sqrt{3x+25}}{x} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{(5-\sqrt{3x+25})(5+\sqrt{3x+25})}{x(5+\sqrt{3x+25})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{5}^{2}-{(\sqrt{3x+25})}^{2}}{x(5+\sqrt{3x+25})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{25-(3x+25)}{x(5+\sqrt{3x+25})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{-3x}{x(5+\sqrt{3x+25})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{-3}{5+\sqrt{3x+25}} \\  & =\frac{-3}{5+\sqrt{3(0)+25}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
